texts.preamble: Prabhanshu Dwivedi vs Mp State Civil Supplies Corporation on 16 July, 2025 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Vivek Jain On The 16th Of July, 2025 Writ Petition No. 19575 of 2025 Prabhanshu Dwivedi Versus Mp State Civil Supplies Corporation And Others Appearance: Shri Siddharth Gulatee Senior Advocate with Shri Dharmes Advocate for the petitioner. Shri Vivek Ranjan Pandey, Advocate for the respondent No Order
texts.facts: By way of present petition, the petitioner has called into question the suspension order Annexure P/1 dated 14.05.2025, whereby the petitioner has been placed under Suspension. The petitioner is working on the substantive post of Junior Assistant but was having charge of Centre Incharge of procurement Centre Shahnagar and Pawai, both in District Panna and run by M.P. State Civil Supply Corporation.
texts.arguments: 2. The learned senior counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner vide order Annexure P/6 was given charge of procurement Centre Pawai on 03.05.2022 and thereafter on 03.08.2022 he was given additional charge of procurement Centre Shahnagar. The petitioner on 11.11.2024 asked for additional charge of procurement Centre Shahnagar vide Annexure P/11 and thereafter vide Annexure P/8, P/9 and P/10 sent in November and December-2024 he requested to relieve himself from the charge of procurement Centre, Shahnagar. It is further argued that the petitioner had 2 WP-19575-2025 informed the Branch Manager of M.P. Ware Housing and Logistics Corporation that rice stored in the ware house is being infested with worms and pests and therefore, it is getting spoilt and the said Corporation (Warehousing Corporation) was requested to carry out pest control activity to save the rice stored in the ware house. 3. It is further argued that the petitioner has been suspended on the prima facie allegation of procurement of substandard rice and not taking any action to ensure safety of rice stored in the ware house. It is contended that the rice was in the custody of Warehouse Corporation and he has no control over the affairs of the said Corporation and that he had requested the Branch Manager of Warehousing Corporation to carry out the past control activity on the rice stored in the Warehouse controlled by it, therefore, the petitioner can not be subjected to penal action for something which was not done by the Warehouse Corporation which are required to be done by the Corporation. 4. It is further argued that the petitioner has been given clean chit in the internal enquiry conducted by the Civil Supplies Corporation vide Annexure P/4 wherein Civil Supplies Corporation has held Prabhanshu Dwivedi vs Mp State Civil Supplies Corporation on 16 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150548209/ 1 that the entire responsibility of rice getting infested by pests and worms lies on the Warehousing Corporation and not on Civil Supply Corporation. It is further argued that the action is taken on the dictat of the Collector he has got no business to issue such instructions to the Civil Supply Corporation because he is not the employer of the petitioner. 5. Per contra, Learned counsel for the respondents/ Civil Supplies 3 WP-19575-2025 Corporation submits that the petition is highly misconceived and the petitioner cannot escape the consequences of his own acts. It is contended that the Civil Supplies Corporation is the owner of the food grains procured by it and Warehousing Corporation is only a custodian of the food grains as it manages and operates Warehouses, therefore, the primary responsibility of the petitioner as an officer and centre incharge of the Civil Supplies Corporation was to have ensured procurement of proper quality of rice and further to ensure that the rice is not destroyed by any elements of nature and pests. It is argued that if the petitioner had come to know that the rice is being infested by pests as far as back in the month November- 2024 then instead of simply writing letters to Warehousing Corporation, on which there is no receipt at all, he could have brought to the notice of Higher Authorities of the Civil Supplies Corporation or of the Warehousing Corporation but could not have been sitting idle by issuing letters to Branch Manager, Warehousing Corporation because responsibility was more than simply writing letters. 6. It is further argued that the Civil Supplies Corporation procures food grains basically for the purpose of public distribution system operated by the State Government. There are three partners in public distribution system so far as the procurement and storage of food grains is concerned. These are firstly, the Civil Supplies Corporation to procure the food grains and is funded by the Government for that purpose. On the second side is Warehousing Corporation which stores the food grains and in the third part is the District Food and Civil Supplies Department of the State Government which is supervised by the Collector of District and the said Department 4 WP-19575-2025 actually distributes the food grains to PDS system. Therefore, it cannot be said that the instructions of the Collector are issued by an authority which had no business or say in the matter because it is the duty of the Food and Civil Supplies department of the State Government to ensure supply of food grains in the District and if pest infested and destroyed rice was being distributed through PDS Shops, then naturally the Collector and food Department of the State would take objection to the issue and write to the Civil Supplies Corporation as well as the Warehousing Corporation to take urgent steps to get their house in order. Therefore, it is not a case where such an authority has recommended something which had no say in the matter, but it is an authority which was a important stake-holder. In the entire turn of events, as many as 527 quintal of rice has been returned from PDS shops and much more rice has been found to be stored in Shahnagar Warehouse which is unfit for consumption and therefore, for huge loss caused to the corporation the petitioner has been placed under suspension and charge-sheet has already been issued to the petitioner within the prescribed time limit and therefore, this Court should not interfere in the suspension order. 7.
